interest: This file provides valuable historical insight into French colonial counter-espionage operations and the surveillance of Japanese activities in Southeast Asia prior to the outbreak of World War II in the Pacific. It illustrates how Japanese commercial concerns, notably Dainan Koosi (Dainan Kōshi), operated under suspicion of acting as fronts for intelligence collection and military reconnaissance in French Indochina. Furthermore, the report's reference to the editor of the local newspaper 'L'Alerte' demonstrates French sensitivity to Japanese propaganda efforts and local collaborative networks in Saigon. The file is also useful for archival historians as it contains the complete distribution chain of a consular despatch (original through quadruplicate) along with internal State Department records-routing ephemera.
overview: This file (894.20251G/1051) from the U.S. State Department records relates to Japanese military activities, intelligence gathering, and espionage in French Indochina during October 1938. The primary document is Despatch No. 7 from American Consul Peter H. A. Flood in Saigon, reporting that French military authorities conducted a raid on October 18, 1938, against the premises of Dainan Koosi, the second-largest Japanese trading firm in Saigon after Mitsui. French authorities seized extensive corporate archives on suspicion of espionage and commenced translating them, an action closely linked to the arrest of the mixed-blood editor of the local newspaper 'L'Alerte' for allegedly aiding Japanese agents. The file preserves the complete set of despatch copies (original, duplicate, triplicate, and quadruplicate), followed by an extraneous court transcript fragment concerning witness testimony and an internal Department of State charge slip routing File 894.202 to Mr. Henry.

subfiles.about: American Consul Peter H. A. Flood reports that French military authorities in Saigon raided the Japanese commercial firm Dainan Koosi on suspicion of espionage.
subfiles.summary: American Consul Peter H. A. Flood reports to the Secretary of State that French military authorities raided the Saigon offices of Dainan Koosi, the largest Japanese trading firm in the city except Mitsui, on the afternoon of October 18, 1938. French officials searched the company's premises and seized a large volume of documents, which were subsequently translated to uncover suspected Japanese espionage operations. The raid followed the arrest of the editor of the Saigon newspaper 'L'Alerte' on other charges, with authorities anticipating disclosures regarding his assistance to Japanese intelligence agents. The sub-file comprises the signed original airmail despatch along with its duplicate, triplicate, and quadruplicate carbon copies.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 7 from American Consul Peter H. A. Flood on raid on Japanese firm Dainan Koosi

subfiles.about: A stray court or legal proceeding transcript fragment numbered page 10 regarding materials in the possession of a witness.
subfiles.summary: This single page, numbered 10, contains a repetitive legal transcript passage concerning whether certain materials were or were not 'in the hands of the said Witness'. It appears to be an anomalous, misfiled court transcript fragment that suffered from a typographical or printing stutter. It bears no subject-matter relationship to the consular reporting on French Indochina.
subfiles.title: Transcript fragment regarding witness testimony

It reflects standard internal routing and document management procedures within the Department.
